extracted.intended_audience: students and practitioners of storytelling (screenwriters, literature students, general readers interested in poetics)
extracted.subtask_description: Summarize and apply Aristotle's short study of storytelling (Poetics), which treats elements like unity of plot, reversal of situation, and character in Greek tragedy, comedy, and epic, and is often applied by modern screenwriters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unity of plot
rubrics_metrics.description: Aristotle discusses 'unity of plot' as a central element of storytelling.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mentioned in the context of Greek tragedy, comedy, and epic poetry; the page notes that these principles still apply today and are frequently referenced by modern screenwriters and 'how-to' books.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reversal of situation (peripeteia)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Poetics discusses 'reversal of situation' (a turning point in the plot) as an important dramatic device.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presented as one of the key plot mechanisms within Greek dramatic forms; the summary emphasizes its continuing relevance for contemporary storytellers, including screenwriters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Character
rubrics_metrics.description: Aristotle treats 'character' as a fundamental component of dramatic works.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discussed alongside plot and reversal within the contexts of tragedy, comedy, and epic; the page's summary implies attention to character is part of evaluating or crafting effective stories and is of interest to modern practitioners.
